scenes.title: Abraham welcomes the visitors and Sarah hears the promise

art.alt: Abraham serves three seated visitors beneath a tree, while Sarah listens from the open tent entrance; artistic reconstruction

scenes.caption: Illustrated reconstruction · Genesis 18:1–15

intro.title: Visitors at Mamre
intro.note: Genesis 18:1 introduces Abraham at the tent door in Mamre. The illustration gathers the welcome, meal, and Sarah hearing the promise into a single editorial scene. It does not establish the appearance of these people or a precise campsite.

hotspots.title: Abraham welcomes the visitors
hotspots.note: Abraham runs to meet the three men and offers water, rest, and food. The visible visitors help explain the welcome described in Genesis 18:2–5.

hotspots.title: Abraham serves the meal
hotspots.note: Sarah prepares cakes, a young man prepares the calf, and Abraham serves butter, milk, and the prepared calf beneath the tree. He stands by the visitors while they eat.

detail.alt: Close view of bread cakes, a milk vessel, butter, and prepared meat on a woven cloth; artistic reconstruction

hotspots.title: Sarah hears the promise
hotspots.note: Sarah hears from the tent door that she will have a son. She laughs within herself because of their age, and the Lord questions her response. The doorway matters because she listens there.

scenes.title: The pledge Judah gives

art.alt: A stone signet, braided bracelets, and a wooden staff arranged on cloth; reconstructed forms of the pledge objects named in Genesis

scenes.caption: Illustrated object study · Genesis 38:18 · Object forms are reconstructed

intro.title: Judah's pledge
intro.note: Genesis names the objects Judah gives as a pledge. The exact design and materials are reconstructed.

hotspots.title: The pledge that identifies Judah
hotspots.note: Tamar asks for Judah’s signet, bracelets, and staff as a pledge. Later, these objects identify him. This object study illustrates their role without depicting the encounter described in the verse.

detail.alt: The signet, bracelets, and wooden staff shown together as a reconstructed object study

art.alt: The pledge objects are presented to Judah, who responds with recognition; artistic reconstruction of the recognition episode

intro.title: Recognizing the evidence
intro.note: The returned pledge objects connect the accusation with Judah's earlier promise. The staging of this scene is an artistic reconstruction.

hotspots.title: Tamar sends the evidence
hotspots.note: Tamar sends word to Judah, asking him to recognize the signet, bracelets, and staff. These are the objects he gave as a pledge earlier in the chapter.

detail.alt: Detail of the reconstructed signet, bracelets, and staff that identify the pledge

hotspots.title: Judah acknowledges his failure
hotspots.note: Judah recognizes the objects and acknowledges his failure to give Tamar to Shelah his son. The illustration focuses on his recognition and admission.

scenes.title: Balaam, the donkey, and the angel

art.alt: A donkey beside a vineyard wall, Balaam bowing, and a messenger holding a drawn sword in the narrow path; artistic reconstruction

scenes.caption: Illustrated reconstruction · Numbers 22:21–35 · Appearance and setting are illustrative

intro.title: Balaam, the donkey, and the angel
intro.note: The donkey sees the angel before Balaam does. This single illustration brings together the encounter’s adjacent moments; it is not an ancient map.

hotspots.title: The donkey turns aside from the sword
hotspots.note: The donkey sees the angel with a drawn sword, turns aside, and presses against the wall before falling down. Balaam strikes it because he does not yet see what it sees.

hotspots.title: The donkey speaks to Balaam
hotspots.note: The LORD opens the donkey’s mouth. It asks Balaam why he has struck it, and he answers. The image identifies the speaking animal without adding words to Scripture.

hotspots.title: Balaam sees the angel blocking the way
hotspots.note: Balaam’s eyes are opened, and he sees the angel with the drawn sword. He bows and is instructed to speak only the word given to him. The messenger’s appearance is reconstructed.

scenes.title: Moses calls Israel to choose life

art.alt: Moses addresses seated listeners under an open sky; the people and setting are artistically reconstructed

scenes.caption: Illustrated reconstruction · Deuteronomy 30:15–20 · Appearance and setting are illustrative

intro.title: Moses calls Israel to choose life
intro.note: Moses places a choice before Israel through his words. The illustration shows the speaker and hearers, without turning life and death into invented geographic routes.

hotspots.title: Moses sets life and good before Israel
hotspots.note: Moses sets life and good against death and evil. He calls Israel to love the LORD, walk in his ways, and keep his commandments. The visible speaker represents this address.

hotspots.title: Israel hears the warning against turning away
hotspots.note: Moses warns what will follow if Israel turns away to serve other gods. The listeners stand for those addressed; their presence does not depict them rejecting the warning.

hotspots.title: Moses calls heaven and earth as witnesses
hotspots.note: Moses calls heaven and earth to record the choice and urges Israel to choose life, love the LORD, obey his voice, and cleave to him. The raised hand and sky illustrate his address.

scenes.title: Jeremiah at the potter’s house

art.alt: A potter shapes a clay vessel at a wheel while Jeremiah watches nearby; reconstructed workshop and objects

scenes.caption: Illustrated reconstruction · Jeremiah 18:1–6 · Appearance and setting are illustrative

intro.title: Jeremiah at the potter’s house
intro.note: Jeremiah watches a potter rework a vessel, and the following words explain the clay comparison. The workshop is an illustration, not a recovered historic location.

hotspots.title: The potter remakes the marred vessel
hotspots.note: The vessel is marred in the potter’s hand, so he makes it again into another vessel. His hands and the clay identify the action Jeremiah observes; the wheel’s design is reconstructed.

hotspots.title: Jeremiah hears the comparison to clay
hotspots.note: The LORD asks whether he can do with the house of Israel as this potter does. The clay in the potter’s hand is the passage’s comparison; the image does not settle every later application.
